result.title: Not Every Mention Is a Claim: Rethinking Object Hallucination Detection in Vision-Language Models
result.summary: Object hallucination in vision-language models (VLMs) is usually measured by checking each object a caption names against the image. Most benchmarks and detectors alike treat every object mention as a claim that the object is present. This assumption fails when a caption names an object without asserting it, as in "a bench for people to sit on", which mentions people without claiming that any are in the image. We call such mentions non-assertive. Treating them as hallucinations inflates the error rates attributed to models that use such language. To separate them from real hallucinations, we introduce NAME-Bench (Non-Assertive Mention Evaluation Benchmark), 25,497 object mentions from captions that five VLMs generate for COCO images. Each mention is labelled concrete (asserted and present), hallucinated (asserted and absent), or non-assertive, and non-assertive mentions are further divided into four subtypes: depictive, purpose, negation and hedged. All the hallucination detectors that we evaluate flag non-assertive mentions as hallucinations, at rates between 14% and 80%. Adding non-assertive mentions to detector training as negatives largely corrects this on LLaVA-1.5. On the four newer VLMs, a comparable correction takes five to ten times more data, and the detectors then catch fewer real hallucinations. These findings show that current detectors conflate mentioning an object with asserting it, and that this conflation is harder to undo on the four newer VLMs than on LLaVA-1.5. Hallucination evaluation should therefore separate what a caption asserts from what it merely mentions.

AI.brief_summary: 论文指出目标幻觉检测默认「提到某物体」就等于「断言该物体存在」，由此构建 NAME-Bench（25,497 条来自五个 VLM 对 COCO 图像描述中的物体 mention，标注为 concrete、hallucinated 与 non-assertive，后者再分 depictive、purpose、negation、hedged 四类），评测现有检测器并用 non-assertive mention 作为负样本训练加以纠正。
AI.relevance_reason: 属于 VLM 视觉证据与输出归因的诊断与基准：其「提及 vs 断言」标注可供核查判断模型回答是否真正依赖视觉内容、而非语言模板，但全文不涉及 latent 推理状态或状态生成，联系需进一步确认。
